doc.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021

title: The whisper room and surviving lockdown
summary: Her soundproof booth in the apartment and how she and her wife worked through lockdown.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh my God I’m definitely patting myself on the back for being able to troubleshoot stuff over Zoom. I do have a whisper room in our apartment in Brooklyn, which is a little soundproof, not quite soundproof but a booth like you used to see in a studio, it’s a vocal booth, that I bought pre-pandemic because I had complaints from a neighbor in our apartment building. And so I got it three months before Covid hit. Then when Covid hit you could not buy one of those. Yeah. So my wife works for the New York City Health Department so she was working from home, she was activated to work on emergency response stuff. So she was working from home, I was working in that booth teaching kids. That’s how we survived, that’s how we survived the last year. It was obviously very intense at that place.
Now I can see why that duo gig with ten people in the audience felt so good.

Yes. Exactly. I’ve been playing in a booth for so long. And I have to say it’s really good sound in there, I’ve actually dug it. It’s — I’ve never had — I’ve always wanted one, to be honest. Because it’s great, you go in there, you shut the door, and you practice. It’s like going to an office instead of — you know, so I do like it and it is actually a good sound in there and I like that I’m not disturbing a ton of people. I can just go in there and just do what I want to do. So, yeah.
